fields.meta_title: Employee Training Form for Training Records | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an employee training form that records who trained, who signed off, and when each certification is due again. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Training Form With Sign-Offs and Due Dates
fields.hero_description: Build an employee training form that saves each course and its trainer sign-off to a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: A sign-in sheet proves someone was in the room. This form records what they learned and when it is due again.
fields.feature_1:
Fields for the training you run

Describe your courses, such as forklift checks or a new point-of-sale system. Emergent builds a form that asks for the course, the date, the trainer, and the final result.
fields.feature_2:
Trainer sign-off on the same screen

The trainer signs on a phone or tablet the moment the employee finishes. The app captures that signature with the trainer's name and the date, next to the course it covers.
fields.feature_3:
Due dates worked out from the last session

Set how long each course stays current, such as 12 months for a ladder safety course. The app adds that period to the last session date and lists every record due next month.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders before anyone falls behind

Email or Slack an employee when a course comes due in 30 days, and copy the manager once the date passes. Each reminder links back to the form for that exact course.
fields.feature_5:
Every record in one table you own

Each submission lands in a database you own, one row per employee and course. Filter by person or course to see who finished the March portal session and who did not.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to take

On paid plans, export the full app to your GitHub repository and host it on servers of your own. Keep building on it alongside the HR system you already run every day.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Records Behind a Trained Crew
fields.tab_content_1:
Rosa is due back for evaluation by June 10, 2029

Pell Creek Freight trains its forklift operators in pairs. Trainer Dale Merriman records Rosa Tavener's training on June 9 and her evaluation on June 10, then signs the form on the dock tablet. OSHA calls for an evaluation of each operator at least once every three years. Her record sets the next one for June 10, 2029.
fields.tab_content_2:
One shop task left before Felix works alone

Felix Arango started at Spoke and Ash Cycles in May. Shop lead Nadia Ocampo signs each of the 5 tasks on his record once he shows it. Four of the 5 carry her signature: brakes, wheels, drivetrains, and suspension. E-bike diagnostics is still open. Until it is signed, Felix stays paired on those repairs.
fields.tab_content_3:
Reminders go to 4 staff who have not finished

Wexford Lane Accounting switched client portals in February. Staff have until March 13 to finish a 45-minute session on it and log it on the training form. By March 10, 18 of the 22 have. The app emails the other 4 a reminder with a link to the session, Maren Yates among them.
fields.tab_content_4:
On October 1, Owen has 6 of his 16 hours

Bracken Hill Electric gives each electrician a yearly goal of 16 training hours. Each course logged on the form adds to that person's total. Anyone under 8 hours on October 1 goes on a list emailed to ops manager Hollis Grady. Owen Pickard has 6, from a 4-hour code update class and a 2-hour arc flash refresher.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Employee Training Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an employee training form that records each signed session and shows what comes due.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the fields every record needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give each course a renewal period
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every course you run, such as forklift, ladder safety, or a new software rollout. Note who teaches each one and how long it stays current. That list becomes the course menu on the form and the start of every record.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask who was trained, on which course and date, who taught it, and whether they passed. Add a field for hours if you track a yearly goal. Leave job performance ratings off it, and let this form record training only.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose who signs each record: the trainer alone, or the trainer and the employee. A trainer's signature shows who vouched for the skill. For hands-on work, list each task on its own line, and the trainer signs them one at a time as the employee shows them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick how long each course counts, such as 12 months or 3 years. The app adds it to the last completion date and sets the next due date. A course with no renewal, like a one-time orientation, stays complete once it is signed.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the course list, the fields, the sign-off rules, and the renewal periods into one prompt. Emergent builds the employee training form, the database behind it, and a table to filter by person or course. Change any of it later in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Remind employees 30 days before a course comes due, and email their manager when a date passes. Connect Slack if your crews read it more than email. Send a monthly list of upcoming renewals to the person who books the classes.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Log one real session as a test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Record a session that already happened, with the real trainer signing on a tablet. Check that the row lands under the right course with the right next due date. Then move the date back a year and confirm the reminder goes out.

faq_plan.q: What is an employee training form?
faq_plan.a: An employee training form is the record that an employee completed a piece of training. It names the employee, the course, the date, and who delivered it. It can also carry a signature and the date the training is due again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an employee training form?
faq_plan.a: List the courses you run, then decide what each record holds and who signs it. Describe all of that in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. You get a working form, with every record saved to a table and each due date set from the renewal periods you gave.

faq_plan.q: Is an employee training form template enough to track renewals?
faq_plan.a: Not on its own. An employee training form template works when you run one course and only need a signed record of it. Build your own once you track renewals, task sign-offs, or yearly hours, because a static template cannot work out a due date. Emergent builds the form from a description of your courses, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Should an employee training form rate how well someone does the job?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep the training form to what was taught, when, by whom, and whether the employee passed. Put ratings of day-to-day work on an employee evaluation form instead. Link the two records by employee ID, and a manager can read someone's training history next to their last review.

faq_plan.q: Can one employee training form handle several different courses?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the courses in a dropdown and give each one its own fields and renewal period. A forklift record asks for an evaluation date, while a software session needs only a completion date. Every record still lands in the same table, and you can filter it by course.

faq_plan.q: What fields does an employee training form need for forklift operators?
faq_plan.a: OSHA's certification for each forklift operator must include the name of the operator, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and the identity of whoever performed the training or evaluation. Make those four required fields. The truck type and the trainer's signature are useful additions of your own.

faq_plan.q: Does the employee need to sign the employee training form?
faq_plan.a: Only when the record has to show that the employee took part. A trainer's signature shows someone checked the skill, and the employee's own signature adds proof of attendance. When you need a signed statement that someone read and understood the material, use a separate training acknowledgment form. Built apps can capture e-signatures for either one.

faq_plan.q: How do I log hours on an employee training form toward a yearly goal?
faq_plan.a: Add an hours field to every course and set a goal for each role, such as 20 hours a year for supervisors. The app totals each person's hours for the year and can flag anyone behind on a date you choose. Built apps can also sync those totals to your HR or payroll system through its API.

faq_plan.q: Can an employee training form double as a training log?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Each submitted form is one row, so the table of all submissions is your training log. Filter it by date for a session-by-session view, or by employee for one person's full history. Emergent keeps that table in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can an employee training form also collect feedback on the session?
faq_plan.a: It can, but keep the two apart. The training form is a record of completion, and opinions mixed into it make that record harder to read later. Send a short training feedback form after each session instead, and tie each response to its course to compare sessions over time.
